about: Unified events conformance (#464): one list both the real runtimes and the SDK testing tools are checked against. Format: docs/design-events-protocol-2026-10-18.en.md §13; the cases of §13.3 come first, then the ones added to cover every rule.

Real runtimes: crates/rutis-loader/tests/events_conformance.rs (rows of one rutis host, its runtimes, and a second node). Testing tools, the cases without `tool: false` whose rows are all at the root (the tools load no row into a scope): go/rutis/rutistest/events_conformance_test.go, swift/rutis/Tests/SelfTest/EventsConformanceTests.swift (RutisTest), kotlin/rutis/rutis-conformance/src/test/kotlin/arcships/rutis/conformance/EventsConformanceTest.kt. The file is checked for shape by crates/rutis-bridge/tests/events_expected.rs.

Languages (`only` / `except`): rust (the host's Rust plugin), node (a Cordis plugin in the Node runtime), node-leaf (a leaf plugin in the Node runtime), bun, python, go, swift, kotlin (the Kotlin SDK's jvm target). Fixtures: node/rutis-runtime/test/fixtures/conformance-events{,-e,-f}/ (Cordis) and conformance-events-leaf{,-e,-f}.mjs, bun/rutis-bun/test/fixtures/conformance-events{,-e,-f}.ts, python/rutis/tests/fixtures/conformance_events{,_e,_f}.py, go/rutis/internal/fixtures/plugins/conformance (served by go/rutis/internal/fixtures/runtime; one plugin provides every emitter undeclared, its sync method on the wire `dispatchSync`), swift/rutis/Sources/RutisFixturePlugins/ConformanceEvents.swift (served by RutisConformance; as Go), kotlin/rutis/rutis-conformance/src/main/kotlin/arcships/rutis/conformance/plugins/ConformanceEvents.kt (likewise: one plugin provides every emitter undeclared, `dispatchSync`), and the Rust plugin of crates/rutis-loader/tests/events_conformance.

Scopes: each scope path is one instance of its group, created once; t2's group is `team`, not `tenant`, so that rows placed in t1 are not copied into t2 (a loader instance copies its group's rows). A listener's scope is a descriptor for filters; delivery is by name on one flat bus, as in Cordis, so every listener hears every event regardless of its scope.

Additions to the format of §13.2: a listener's `fails` ({name, message}: its row's apply throws that error, after registering nothing); a listener's `inject` (service names: the row's own `inject` list, as a configuration gives it: `rutis/row-failed-gated` checks that such a row, behind a gate in a Cordis runtime, fails with its apply's error as `rutis/row-failed` does, #584); `typed: "unit"` (a Rust unit struct event); `observesDispatch` (a Cordis listener row that also logs `<label>:dispatch:<mode>` from its internal/dispatch for each dispatch of the case's name); the filter `{"throws": {name, message}}` (the predicate throws); the step `{"update": label}` (the row's config changes, so it registers again); and `expect` on a `load` step. Rust events cross by serde without a declaration, so there is no NoWire case.

Expectations, strictly: a step without `throws` or `cancelled` requires every dispatch that ends in it to succeed. `cancelled: true`: the dispatch ends with its emitter's language's cancellation (Python `CancelledError`, Go `Canceled`, Swift `CancellationError`, Kotlin `CancellationException`, the Rust fixture's `Cancelled`). `reported` entries ({label, name, filter?}): exactly one §5.6 line about the step's event names that row (`in row <label>`, or the dispatcher's `in runtime <its runtime>` / `in node <peer>`) with that error name; `filter: true` for a filter's line (`rutis: filter of <name> from row <label>`). `logLacks` (and `reported`) are checked again a moment after the rest held. A `$` tag that does not parse is an error of the file. `toolCases`: how many cases each testing tool runs (crates/rutis-bridge/tests/events_expected.rs checks it against the cases; each tool checks it ran that many).

The rows: plugin `conformance-events`, one row per participant, keyed by its label; its config is the participant as resolved by the runner (name, kind and log filled in). It injects `events-log`, a host service: add(entry) sync; filter(description) sync (logs `filter:<row>` and keeps the description for `filterSees`); wait(entry) async (resolves once entry is logged, for `cancel`). Emitter rows (labelled e or f) load the plugin `conformance-events-e` or `conformance-events-f` (Python `conformance_events_e` / `_f`): the same plugin, declaring only its own `emitter-<label>` (a declared service is exported whether the row provides it or not), with dispatch(spec) async and dispatch_sync(spec) sync (for bail). `conformance-events` itself declares nothing.
